page.layout: One column of text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top. Division heads "EXERCITATIO II." and "CAP. I." centred, with subtitles below them. Page number at top right. Catchword "Dei" at bottom right, signature "Q 3" at bottom centre.

main_text.l: voluntates ad omnes actus suos? Sed quaero, an sit
certitudo actuum liberorum futurorum ante-
cedenter ad decreta Dei? Si sit, tum etiam est
necessitas fundamentalis & entitativa in iis an-
tecedenter ad Dei decreta: Erg. Deus non
habet in sua potestate aliter decernere actus li-
beros, quam sunt antecedenter ad Dei decreta.
Eligat jam Iesuita utrum Deum, an homines
velit necessitari ad actus liberos. 2. Videtur
sequi hinc duas esse necessitates actuum libero-
rum, unam antecedenter, aliam consequen-
ter ad Dei decreta: at quid opus est Deus
praescire in actu approbativo & permissivo fu-
turos actus liberos, si jam sunt illi actus Deo
certissimi ante omnes Dei voluntatis approba-
tivos & permissivos actus? Sed nos Arrianis
primis hujus scientiae authoribus, ut observat
Did. Alvarez, & novatoribus hisce relinqua-
mus hoc mysterium pudendum.
EXERCITATIO II.
De notionibus divinae voluntatis.
CAP. I.
AGnoscunt unanimiter Scholastici hanc di-
stinctionem: circa objectum ipsius non
nihil discrepant. D. Bannes ait, probabile esse Alexan.
1. quod fit in Deo formaliter actus volendi bo-
num, qui non compleatur. Alexander Halensis,
Cajetanus, Driedo, & alii agnoscunt non esse Dei
[?] Note marks and references are printed in the margin; see the notes below.

page.notes: The right margin carries the references: "Bannes tom. 1. q. 19. art. 6", "Alexan. 1.", "p. q. 36. art. 2", "Cajet. in. 1.", "Tim. 2.", "Driedo de conc. 1." and "q. p. 4." Several are abbreviated and uncertain, so the exact wording is marked where it is doubtful. The first word "AGnoscunt" starts with a large initial A. The word "distinctionem" is broken as "di-" / "stinctionem": the first letter of the second line is an ornamental form and is read as s. The title "Cap. I." and its subtitle are set in centred type. The short line "Eligat jam Iesuita utrum Deum, an homines" carries a small mark after "homines" that may be a printing sign; it is left as "homines". The paragraph beginning "voluntates" continues from the previous page.
